chunks: And it has been narrated from al-Sadiq عليه السلام that he said:
"A loan is an excellent thing: if he becomes able, he repays you; and if he becomes unable, you count it as part of the zakat."

key_terms.أَعْسَرَ: became unable or fell into hardship
key_terms.الزَّكَاةِ: the obligatory alms-tax in whose place this amount may be reckoned
key_terms.الْقَرْضُ: a loan given to another person

ai.seo_question: Why is giving a loan considered a good deed in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith praises giving a loan as a virtuous and beneficial act. If the borrower can repay, the lender recovers the amount; if the borrower cannot, the amount may be counted toward zakat, showing both financial wisdom and compassion.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1601 - It has been narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he said:
"Loaning is a good deed. If the borrower is able to repay, they will do so; and if they are unable, you can count it as part of your Zakat."
